proof_summary: Lucas congruences split the defining sums into cancelling parts to show both sequences vanish modulo \(p\) throughout \(p\le n\le2p-2\); at \(n=p-1\), an alternating geometric sum gives the first boundary value, while vanishing of central binomial coefficients leaves only the midpoint term for the second. Reversing the columns of each Hankel matrix makes it triangular with this boundary value on the diagonal, and combining its determinant with the reversal sign \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) yields the two results.
